trade_from: The same class as the bare body under the plate. See DarkKnightBare.json.
note: A character is an assembly, not a mesh. MU has no body model - player.bmd holds meshes=0, only the skeleton and the actions - so what stands here is the five worn parts, each authored already positioned in body space. Nothing is placed by this file; the parts are simply loaded together at the origin.
rig: player.bmd, beside this file. Not used yet: these are bind-pose parts.
hands_note: Held, not worn, and the difference is the whole of how they are attached. A worn part is skinned - its vertices bind to bone names and it bends at the elbow with the arm. A held item is rigid: MU takes one bone's transform and places the whole model at it, and sending a weapon through the skinning path binds its vertices to every bone whose name happens to match and draws it stretched across the character.
hands_from: The player rig carries bones made for the purpose - knife_gdf for the right hand and hand_bofdgne01 for the left - and they sit where a grip belongs rather than at the wrist joint. That is why the grip is identity here: no rotation, no offset, because the socket bone and the item's own bone orientation have already decided the placement between them. The old client's MuAttachment.cs records three separate attempts to derive a correction for hanging weapons off Bip01 R Hand instead, each landing somewhere different because each was fitting the same wrong premise.
hands_why_these: A shield is the off-hand item: it takes Weapon[1] and goes in the hand a one-handed weapon leaves free. MuShields.cs lists the Plate Shield as Knight-only, and the Kris is a one-handed sword, so this is a loadout a Dark Knight could actually carry. It is also what picks the animation - the weapon decides the stance and the shield has no say in it, so a one-handed sword gives Stop 4 and Walk 17, which is what the viewer was already playing.
